The headphone jack will take a lot longer to replace. By switching to a digital output, few to no audio players will be compatible with your device. Every single set of headphones, earbuds, or vintage audio gear will require not only a USB-C/digital input, but a digital audio converter (DAC). Right now, all phones have these built-in because the headphone jack requires an analog signal. By not having a DAC, the digital to analog signal conversion needs to occur elsewhere. This would lead to a large number of battery-powered DAC/Amplifiers that would be necessary to convert the digital signal and then power the headphones/earbuds. As is, most modern cellphones have pretty weak amplifiers.

However some phone makers know that people who care about audio and are doing some pretty innovative things. By offering premium DAC's in their phones (like LG announced today) or HTC's 10, the customers who have invested in audio systems have devices that perfectly fit their needs.
